title: Sampling Distributions & Standard Error
interviewAnswer: A sampling distribution describes how an estimator would vary across repeated samples. Standard error measures that estimator uncertainty; it is not the standard deviation of the raw observations.
keyPoints: Estimator variability shrinks with more information/sample size.
SE and population SD answer different questions.
why: Sampling Distributions & Standard Error appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Estimator variability shrinks with more information/sample size.
deepDive: A sampling distribution describes how an estimator would vary across repeated samples. Standard error measures that estimator uncertainty; it is not the standard deviation of the raw observations. SE and population SD answer different questions. Sampling design affects uncertainty. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: The mean order value may have SD €40 across orders but a much smaller SE for the estimated population mean.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Sampling Distributions & Standard Error make?
How would you validate or debug Sampling Distributions & Standard Error in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
